title.en: Gupta trade, administration, art and decline

text.en:
Anu saw the stone carvings of the Gupta temple at Deogarh.
"They were skilled builders," said her teacher.

The Guptas, founded by Sri Gupta and made great by Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Chandragupta II, ruled most of north India. Gold coins show a rich economy and trade with Rome and South-East Asia.
The empire was divided into provinces with officers, and the king was supported by councils. Art flourished: temples, sculptures and the Ajanta paintings.
Attacks by the Huns, weak rulers and rising regional powers led to the decline of the empire.

problem.en: Why did the Gupta Empire decline?

prompt.en: A friend says the Guptas ruled only a small village. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They ruled most of north India.

points.en: The Guptas had a rich economy.
Huns and weak rulers ended the empire.
